# task-hub

> Your local coding agents turn each GitHub Project card you move to Ready into a reviewed PR.
> Ready に移した GitHub Project のカードを、手元のエージェントがレビュー済みの PR にする。

task-hub is a command-line tool (`task`) for macOS, with Windows support. It is written in Python with the standard library only, under the MIT license.
It is for people who build with GitHub Issues and PRs and run an agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Kiro, and others) on their own Mac.
You move a card to Ready and merge the PR. task-hub and your agents do the rest: implement, test, review in a fresh context, open the PR, and sort out why a task stopped.
Each card leaves its report and review verdict on the Issue, and its column shows where it is.
This file is the landing page (site/index.html) as text. The docs are in Japanese. The example data is made up.

## One card, layer by layer

The example card is `you/tasks#12` "Add a search box to the notes list", worked in `you/notes-app`.
Its acceptance criteria: it finds notes by title or body, ignoring case (`milk` finds `Buy Milk`), and has tests.
The first review says `needs changes` (the search was case-sensitive); the second says `pass`.

The color of each layer says who does the work: you, task-hub's code, or an agent (an LLM).

1. GitHub Project card (you): you move the card from Backlog to Ready, the go-ahead. Here: #12 waits in Ready on the board.
2. task-hub runner (task-hub): `task watch` reads the board every minute and starts the card in a free slot. Here: `task list` shows #12 as `In progress › agent`.
3. Worktree (task-hub): one branch and one working folder per card, apart from every other card. Here: the branch `task/12`.
4. Local coding agent (agent): edits files, runs the tests, and writes a report. It never touches git. Here: the search box change and `.task-report.md`.
5. Fresh-context review (agent): another agent checks each acceptance criterion and sends the work back if one fails. Here: `needs changes`, then `pass`.
6. PR (task-hub): task-hub pushes, opens the PR, and writes the report and the verdict on the Issue. Here: the PR on `you/notes-app`; the card is In review.
7. Merge queue (task-hub): brings the approved PR up to date with its base and waits for its checks, one per repository at a time. Here: `task merge 12` and the `wait for merge` column.
8. Merge (you; task-hub under `[autopilot]`): the PR goes in, the Issue closes, and the worktree is cleaned up. Cards waiting on it start. Here: the card is Done.

An LLM does only three jobs: implement, review, and sort out why a task stopped. Code decides when to start, when to notify, and when to clean up.

## What it does

- One PR per task: each card gets one branch, one worktree, and one PR. Up to 5 run at the same time, on branches named `task/<id>`.
- Pre-PR review: an agent in a fresh context checks each acceptance criterion. It sends the work back 2 times at most by default. With `review_mode = goldfish`, two viewpoints that skip the report check it.
- Goal check: `task check <id>` has agents that know only the Goal and the code say GO or NO-GO. A NO-GO comes with wording to add. With `readiness = require`, a card without a GO does not start.
- Stop recovery: a run that stops on a crash or a restart resumes once, from where it stopped. A run that hits the usage limit waits for the reset time, then goes on from the same place.
- Blocked triage: an agent sorts out why a task stopped and comments on the Issue. Add the answer to the Goal, move the card to Ready, and the same PR continues.
- Merge queue: `task merge` approves a PR; the queue brings it up to date with its base, waits for its checks, and merges it. An agent fixes conflicts. One PR per repository at a time.
- Agent choice: any agent CLI with a non-interactive mode works. task-hub does git, the PR, and the Issue comments in code, so every agent makes the same kind of PR.
- Alerts and cost: In review, Blocked, long runs, and runs over budget show as OS notifications and on ntfy. No LLM is used. Tokens and cost per launch come from the agent CLI's own records (`task stats`).

## Start in three steps

You need macOS (Windows: docs/windows.md), Python 3.10 or later, git, `gh` logged in, and at least one agent CLI logged in.

1. Install a clone of its own (`~/.local/bin` must be on your PATH):
   `git clone https://github.com/jyoka/task-hub.git ~/.local/lib/task-hub` and
   `ln -sfn ~/.local/lib/task-hub/bin/task ~/.local/bin/task`
2. Let `gh` use Projects: `gh auth refresh -s project`
3. Write `~/.config/task-hub/config.ini` (`[board] project = <owner>/<project number>`, `issues = <owner>/<repository that holds the Issues>`; `[runner] agent = claude`, `reviewer = agent`), check it with `task list`, then run `task`.

Commands for the first day:

- `task list`: see the open cards (read only)
- `/task`, `/chief` in your agent: register a task from a chat (install the skills; the names differ per agent: docs/setup.md)
- `task new --title ... --repo owner/name --goal ...`: register a task from the terminal
- `task start <id>`: approve a Backlog card, or run a Blocked card again
- `task watch`: start Ready cards on their own, every minute
- `task show <id>`: read the report and the verdict
- `task log <id>`: see the end of the run's output on this machine (`--full` for all of it)
- `task help`: see every flag

## Compare

Two kinds of tools are close to task-hub: cloud agents you assign a GitHub Issue to, and board apps that run agents on your machine.
task-hub keeps the board on GitHub (a GitHub Project) and runs the agents on your Mac, with the agent CLIs you already log in to.
What task-hub adds before the merge: a fresh-context review of each acceptance criterion (with `[runner] reviewer = agent`; 2 send-backs at most by default), a resume after a crash, an agent that sorts out why a task is Blocked, and a merge queue (with `[merge] queue = on`, off by default; one PR per repository at a time).
The other tools' review, recovery, and merge features were not checked, so this page says nothing about them.
